subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which slice of #35203, if any, should OpenClaw core sponsor now versus routing to plugins or narrower follow-up issues?
rationale: VISION.md guards against heavy default orchestration while the RFC adds shared state, memory visibility, and budget config surfaces that require product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Keep As Umbrella, Split Slices
options.body: Leave #35203 open for design input and create scoped follow-ups only for maintainer-sponsored layers such as budget enforcement, blackboard API seams, or teleconference-adjacent memory sharing.

options.title: Route Most Work To Plugins
options.body: Treat capability profiling, blackboard, and layered memory as plugin/ClawHub work unless a missing core API seam is identified.

options.title: Sponsor Core Budget Governance First
options.body: Prioritize only the token reservation/enforcement layer in core because it addresses production cost risk without committing to the full orchestration stack.

recommendation.title: Keep As Umbrella, Split Slices
recommendation.body: Leave #35203 open for design input and create scoped follow-ups only for maintainer-sponsored layers such as budget enforcement, blackboard API seams, or teleconference-adjacent memory sharing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already gave the closest maintainer-facing scoping guidance on the narrower teleconference and handoff relatives.
